name: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
problem: Existing serving systems reserve a large, fixed, CONTIGUOUS maximum sequence-length block of KV memory per request, so most of that memory is wasted whenever the actual sequence is shorter - capping throughput well below what the hardware could reach.
mechanism: Borrow virtual memory paging. The KV cache is divided into fixed-size blocks that need not be contiguous; a block table per request records which physical blocks belong to it, and attention kernels read through the block table. Logical blocks are what the scheduler allocates and what the block hash identifies, so a request only consumes as many blocks as it has actually filled. The same indirection enables sharing a prefix across requests (copy-on-write) and within a request (beam/parallel sampling).
speedup_reported: Paper's own claims (abstract): vLLM improves throughput of popular LLMs by 2-4x AT THE SAME LEVEL OF LATENCY vs state-of-the-art systems (named: FasterTransformer and Orca), with the improvement more pronounced for longer sequences, larger models and more complex decoding algorithms. This is the strongest and most-cited serving claim in the batch and the baseline is named.
